JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
Sri. Praveena vs Sri. Hanumantha.

T on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160309401/
1 2.

The facts leading to the filing of the instant petition are that on 23.05.2017 at about 5.00 p.m.,
when the petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02EX0533 near Neelagiri Garden, Abbigere Main road, Bengaluru City, at that time the rider of Bajaj KTM motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02JF0230 came in a rash & negligent manner and dashed against his motorcycle.
Due to the terrific impact the petitioner sustained grievous injuries for which he has taken treatment by spending substantial amount.
The accidental injuries have caused permanent disability to him.
The respondents being the owner and insurer of Bajaj KTM motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02JF0230 are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Despite due service of notice of the petition upon him, the respondent No.1 failed to appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 filed written statement admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Bajaj KTM motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02JF 0230.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Negligence on the part of the rider of its insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the petitioner who was riding motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02EX0533 without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the alleged accident.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the Bajaj KTM motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02JF0230 did not possess valid &
effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

On account of willful breach of the terms &
conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non compliance of Sec's 134(c) & 158 (6) of the MV Act, 1988 is pleaded.
Rest of the petition averments are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a road traffic accident on 23.05.2017 at about 8.00 p.m, near Neelagiri Garden, Abbigere Main road,
Bengaluru City and sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligence of the rider of Bajaj KTM motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02JG0230 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What Order or award ?
5.
The petitioner got examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 13 were marked on his behalf.

Dr.
Nagaraj.
B.N s/o B.K.N. Swamy, Orthopedic Surgeon, Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru was examined as PW.2.
Ex's .P14 & 15 were marked through this witness.
The respondent No.2 did not choose to adduce any evidence on its behalf.
Sri. Praveena vs Sri. Hanumantha.

T on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160309401/
2 6.
Arguments were addressed on both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows : Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 7. ISSUE NO.1 : The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Sri.Santhosh.U, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed chargesheet against the rider of Bajaj KTM motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02JF0230 for the offences punishable u/s's 279 & 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of Bajaj KTM motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02JF0230.
8.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 drew the attention of this Court as to the delay in lodging the complaint.
Indeed there is delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint.
But in view of the ratio laid down in the decision reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, delay in lodging the FIR cannot be a ground to deny justice to the victim.

Even otherwise, when the injured was admitted to the hospital for taking treatment due to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident, it was the bounden duty of the hospital authorities to send the MLC intimation to the concerned police station, who were duty bound to rush to the hospital, record the statement of the injured and register the case at the earliest.
For their fault petitioner cannot be blamed.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
9. ISSUE NO.2 :

As per the medical records petitioner has sustained the following injuries : (i)
severe head injury (ii) right zygoma fracture (iii) left clavicle fracture, which are opined to be grievous in nature.
The aforestated injuries were treated conservatively and the petitioner was discharged on 04.06.2017.
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of Bajaj KTM motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02JF0230.

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
10. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Nagaraj. B.N as PW.2, who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him,
he found that petitioner has total permanent physical disability of the left arm at 29%
and whole body disability at 10%.
It is relevant to note that Clavicle or collar bone is a slender S shaped bone approximately 6 inches that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum.
Together with the shoulder blade, it makes up the Sri. Praveena vs Sri. Hanumantha.

T on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160309401/
3 shoulder griddle.
To put it differently, clavicle bone is not a separate component of the arm but just a supporting bone.
It is in this view of the matter, no disability is prescribed for clavicle fracture in the Government of India guidelines 2018.
Despite of it, PW.2 has assessed the whole body disability of the petitioner at 10% which is totally contrary to the guidelines.
Be that as it may as the clavicle fracture does not lead to any disability the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
11. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

The Discharge summaries issued by Sparsh Hospital and Meggan Hospital, Shivamoga indicate that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospitals for the period from 23.05.2017 to 04.06.2017.
The period of hospitalization of 13 days is thus proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take his care by leaving their duties.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,500/
per day and a sum of Rs.19,500/ (1,500 X 13) which is rounded off to Rs.20,000/
is awarded under this head.
12. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/ under this head.

13. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAIDUP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 5 months.
Therefore this Tribunal deems it expedient to take note of loss of income to the petitioner during the said period.
Accordingly the same is quantified at Rs.8,000/ p.m and a sum of Rs.40,000/ (8,000 X 5) is awarded under this head.
14. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the bills marked at Ex.P13, the petitioner has spent Rs.1,29,301/ towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his crossexamination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,29,301/ which is rounded off to Rs.1,30,000/
towards medical expenses.

15. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
On examination of the petitioner
the doctor witness has noted the following : swelling over the left clavicular region, painful bursa over the swelling and restricted left shoulder movements.

The recent xray of the left clavicle of the petitioner shows :
Sri. Praveena vs Sri. Hanumantha.

T on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160309401/
4 nonunion of the fracture of the clavicle.
A nonunion is a fracture that has failed to heal after several months.
Hence the said bone will be less strong.

Under such circumstances certainly there would be some sort of discomfort which would come in the way of effective discharge of the duties of the petitioner and for that he needs to be compensated suitably.
Having regard to this aspect, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.60,000/ under this head.
16. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.
17. The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Loss of future income due to :  Nil  disability 2
Attendant charges, extra : 20,00000 nutritious food & conveyance charges 3 Pain & sufferings : 50,00000 4 Loss of income during laid : 40,00000 up period 5
Medical expenses : 1,30,00000 6 Loss of future amenities & : 60,000 00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses :  Nil  Total 3,00,00000 18.
INTEREST & LIABILITY:

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a,
is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
19.
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Though the insurance company contended that the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy, no evidence is adduced to prove such breach of terms and conditions of the policy by the first respondent.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Bajaj KTM motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02JF0230 are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
20. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,00,000/ (Rupees Three Lakhs only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.

5
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the aforesaid award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit, the entire award amount together with interest, shall be released to the petitioner by way of Epayment on proper identification and confirmation.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw an award accordingly.
